chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

It is not appropriate for the one in iʿtikāf to leave the mosque except for an unavoidable need; then he should not sit until he returns. And he should not go out for anything except for a funeral or to visit a sick person, and he should not sit until he returns. He said: the iʿtikāf of a woman is like that.

key_terms.اعْتِكَافُ: iʿtikāf, devotional retreat with specific legal conditions
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman, whose iʿtikāf is stated here to follow the same rule
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the required place of iʿtikāf in this context
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفِ: the person performing iʿtikāf, spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.لِجَنَازَةٍ: for a funeral, one of the permitted reasons to leave
key_terms.لِحَاجَةٍ: for a need, meaning a necessary matter that cannot be avoided
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: a sick person, referring to visiting the ill

ai.seo_question: When may a person in iʿtikāf leave the mosque, and do the same rules apply to women?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for the person performing iʿtikāf, restricting خروج from the mosque to unavoidable necessity and requiring prompt return without sitting outside. It also permits leaving for a funeral or visiting a sick person, and states that the ruling for a woman's iʿtikāf is the same.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2099 - It is narrated by Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"It is not appropriate for the one performing i'tikaf to leave the mosque except for an unavoidable necessity, and they should not sit until they return. They should only leave for attending a funeral or visiting a sick person, and even then, they should not sit until they return to the mosque. The i'tikaf of a woman is the same as this."
